nodes.label: bun --cwd apps/learn run <script> prints usage and exits 0, a false pass
nodes.norm_label: bun --cwd apps/learn run <script> prints usage and exits 0, a false pass
nodes.summary: The four root scripts of the fasttrack repo used `bun --cwd apps/learn run <script>`, which on Bun v1.4.2 prints its usage text and exits 0. Every green exit code from those scripts was therefore meaningless: the script never ran.

nodes.label: bun --filter <package> <script> is the genuine workspace script form
nodes.norm_label: bun --filter <package> <script> is the genuine workspace script form
nodes.summary: The replacement wiring for build, typecheck and lint: `bun --filter fasttrack-learn <name>`. Verified exit 0 with real output for typecheck, and a real build completion, so failure propagates instead of being swallowed.

nodes.label: Root bun test discovers the suites that --filter cannot reach
nodes.norm_label: root bun test discovers the suites that --filter cannot reach
nodes.summary: Because apps/learn declares no test script, `--filter` can never run its suites. Running `bun test` from the repo root instead discovers scripts/skills-lib.test.ts and apps/learn/src/lib/*.test.ts: 24 tests across 3 files, 0 failures.

nodes.label: A pipe into tail reports tail's own status, so every wrapped command reads 0
nodes.norm_label: a pipe into tail reports tail's own status, so every wrapped command reads 0
nodes.summary: The first pass measured every exit code through `| tail`, which reports tail's status and is always 0. It was the negative control that exposed this. All five commands were re-run with redirect-to-file plus an explicit `echo $?`.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-fasttrack/2026-09-29 - fix-root-package-scripts [ses_f123039d6ffeRCUrnp5alwgtfd].md:L746] Pipe masking reports tail's status, always 0, so all five exits were re-measured with redirect to file

nodes.label: A nonexistent script name as a negative control proves the wiring propagates failure
nodes.norm_label: a nonexistent script name as a negative control proves the wiring propagates failure
nodes.summary: `bun --filter fasttrack-learn nonexistent-script` exits 1 with error: Script not found. This is the control that distinguishes real wiring from another false pass, and it is what caught the pipe-masking error in the same pass.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-fasttrack/2026-09-29 - fix-root-package-scripts [ses_f123039d6ffeRCUrnp5alwgtfd].md:L27] Temporarily break nothing; a bad script name proves failure without touching the tree

nodes.label: embed_clipboard_delete bumps a bookkeeping row to pending instead of removing it
nodes.norm_label: embed_clipboard_delete bumps a bookkeeping row to pending instead of removing it
nodes.summary: The real mechanism of the embedding leak was not a missing delete. The AFTER DELETE trigger sets revision=revision+1, embedded_revision=NULL, attempts=0, next_attempt_at=0 on the metadata row instead of deleting it, so 2020 of 2521 rows pointed at entries that no longer existed. Fixed with a set-based prune across all three delete paths.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - linux-snippets [ses_f1b2d101dffeuO6rGxfkgxpEkx].md:L10297] The bump was kept because a revision bump is the correct behaviour for edits

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - linux-snippets [ses_f1b2d101dffeuO6rGxfkgxpEkx].md:L4563] The worker query is a LEFT JOIN rooted at clipboard_history, so orphan rows are never selected, retried or reaped

nodes.label: loadMore caps with slice(length - 200) and drops the newest already-loaded entries
nodes.norm_label: loadmore caps with slice(length - 200) and drops the newest already-loaded entries
nodes.summary: pollNewItems keeps slice(0, 200) but loadMore keeps slice(combined.length - 200). Because the backend orders created_at DESC and loadMore appends older pages at the end, the tail slice keeps the oldest 200 and evicts the newest already-loaded ones. With 501 entries this fires on the third scroll; the RED test caught it as `expected 180 to be 200`.

nodes.label: The Magic Menu gates its Telegram button on the telegram_bot_token row, hiding it while the bot is paired
nodes.norm_label: the magic menu gates its telegram button on the telegram_bot_token row, hiding it while the bot is paired
nodes.summary: telegram_bot_token has no row at all while telegram_chat_id, telegram_paired_at and telegram_last_update_id (960287701) all exist. Gating a paired bot's button on the presence of the secret row rather than on pairing state is what hides it.

nodes.label: POST /settings/unset accepted any preference key; its denylist covered only vault_* and mfa_*
nodes.norm_label: post /settings/unset accepted any preference key; its denylist covered only vault_* and mfa_*
nodes.summary: The only traced code path that can delete a preference row outright, and it accepted any key. This matches the live state exactly: 0 rows for the token, 3 sibling preferences present. Fixed with an exact match, 4 regression tests, and a 403 message that names the token.

nodes.label: A mandatory bookkeeping prune turned a successful delete into an error when the table was absent
nodes.norm_label: a mandatory bookkeeping prune turned a successful delete into an error when the table was absent
nodes.summary: Making the embedding prune mandatory meant a missing embedding_metadata table turned delete_clipboard_entry into Err, which silently disabled the moderation worker's auto-delete. The prune is now best-effort with its own regression test.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - linux-snippets [ses_f1b2d101dffeuO6rGxfkgxpEkx].md:L9491] That harness has a bare schema without embedding_metadata, so the prune statement failed with no such table

nodes.label: An insert trigger created the row the purge test asserted was an orphan
nodes.norm_label: an insert trigger created the row the purge test asserted was an orphan
nodes.summary: The T5 test asserted zero embedding rows after a purge and observed one. The single surviving row was legitimate: the prune had removed every orphan correctly. The test expectation was wrong, not the fix.

nodes.label: Retention purge runs only on capture or a preference write, so overdue entries are lazy by design
nodes.norm_label: retention purge runs only on capture or a preference write, so overdue entries are lazy by design
nodes.summary: Three entries older than 7 days survived a 7-day retention setting. The suspected cause, RFC3339 timestamps failing to parse in the DELETE predicate, was disproved by testing the predicate directly. Entries survive until the next capture, so this is lazy enforcement rather than a bug.

nodes.label: run[] commands written CWD-relative fail because the runner executes from the ai-skills repo
nodes.norm_label: run[] commands written cwd-relative fail because the runner executes from the ai-skills repo
nodes.summary: The runner re-executed already-completed steps and reported failures because the plan's commands assumed the project repo root as CWD. All ten commands were rewritten with explicit absolute paths, which changed the runner record to the honest SKIPPED-IDEMPOTENT state.

nodes.label: Verified hot backup, then prune the live SQLite file under a 10s busy timeout with the app running
nodes.norm_label: verified hot backup, then prune the live sqlite file under a 10s busy timeout with the app running
nodes.summary: The backup was taken with SQLite's hot-backup API and verified (integrity_check ok, 501 clipboard rows, 2521 embed rows matching live). The prune then succeeded under WAL with a 10 s busy timeout without closing Snipset: 2020 orphans to 0, 2521 to 501 rows, all 501 live entries untouched.

nodes.label: Self-deadlock from holding the global DB lock in a test
nodes.norm_label: self-deadlock from holding the global db lock in a test
nodes.summary: Reused id. The RED test held the DB lock guard while calling add_clipboard_entry, which re-locks the same mutex, so nextest hung past 20 minutes instead of failing. A RED that hangs is failing for the wrong reason; the guard has to be dropped first.

nodes.label: Zero-subagent compiler policy
nodes.norm_label: zero subagent compiler policy
nodes.summary: Reused id. AGENTS.md forbids delegating any cargo/rustc/clippy/nextest command to a subagent, so T3, T4, T5 and T9 were run inline in the parent over ssh on vps-bcb even though the skill mandates subagent-first execution.

nodes.label: Two tasks touching the same file are overlapping write scopes, so they cannot be dispatched in parallel
nodes.norm_label: two tasks touching the same file are overlapping write scopes, so they cannot be dispatched in parallel
nodes.summary: T4 and T5 both modify clipboard_mutations.rs and T6 and T7 both modify the web loader, so strict non-overlapping workspaces rules out parallelising them. That, plus the compiler policy, is the explicit stated reason for falling below the 10-subagent fan-out floor.

nodes.label: A pure rank_stored kernel was extracted so the untested semantic search path could be covered
nodes.norm_label: a pure rank_stored kernel was extracted so the untested semantic search path could be covered
nodes.summary: embedding_search.rs had no test module at all, so the whole semantic search path was unverified. The filter body was lifted verbatim into a pure rank_stored(), then covered for the two defensive exclusions: dimension-mismatched vectors from a model swap are dropped rather than scored 0.0, and non-finite scores never reach a sort order.

nodes.label: A Snipset-captured screenshot reaches the Magic Menu only if it also reaches the system clipboard
nodes.norm_label: a snipset-captured screenshot reaches the magic menu only if it also reaches the system clipboard
nodes.summary: A copied image does auto-land in the Magic Menu and lazy-loads its thumbnail. Region captures go to activity/worker.rs instead, so the clipboard monitor is the sole writer path. By design, not a defect.
